meta.comment: engine.traffic (planned MOD) inc0 table (f): emergency response time targets, speed-vs-v/c degradation factor, and incident rates by service. Feeds inc4 (isochrone coverage) and the wellbeing coupling (inc5).
meta.unitsConvention: targetMinutes = minutes from dispatch to arrival; incidentsPer1000PopulationPerDay = dispatched-incident count per 1,000 population per day; speedReductionFactor is a dimensionless multiplier applied to free-flow emergency-vehicle speed as a function of the road's v/c ratio (emergency vehicles are NOT immune to congestion, though they partially bypass it via priority/lane-splitting).

services.note: Category 1/2 life-threatening call response target. UK NHS Ambulance Response Programme: Category 1 mean 7 min / 90th centile 15 min nationally; this schema uses a simplified single urban/rural target pending a future percentile-band increment.
services.source: NHS England Ambulance Response Programme (ARP) standards
services.confidenceNote: The NHS category targets are a measured, published national standard; the urban/rural SPLIT applied here (8/15) is this schema's own simplification of the finer NHS percentile structure.
services.turnoutSource: NHS England ARP call-handling/activation guidance: crew mobilisation (dispatch-to-wheels-rolling) target for Category 1 is typically under 2 minutes -- this schema takes 1.5 min as a mid-range derived figure.
services.turnoutConfidenceNote: Derived from the published ARP activation-time guidance band, not a single official statutory turnout figure.

services.note: UK Fire and Rescue Services do not have one single national statutory response target (each Fire & Rescue Authority sets its own Integrated Risk Management Plan target) -- 8/15 min urban/rural mirrors the commonly-published first-appliance attendance target used by multiple UK FRAs (e.g. London Fire Brigade's first-attendance target) as a mapping sanity-check, not a single official national figure.
services.source: UK Fire & Rescue Service published first-attendance targets (multiple FRA IRMPs), order-of-magnitude cross-check
services.confidenceNote: No single UK-wide statutory figure exists; this is a derived cross-FRA order-of-magnitude, not one measured national standard.
services.turnoutSource: UK fire and rescue turnout-time norms (whole-time crews): commonly cited ~60-90 second turnout from alarm to wheels-rolling -- this schema takes 1.0 min as the derived mid-point.
services.turnoutConfidenceNote: Derived from commonly-published UK FRA turnout-time norms for whole-time crews, not one official national statutory figure (retained/on-call crews turn out slower, out of scope for this schema).

services.note: Immediate/Grade 1 response target used by several UK police forces (varies by force); directional placeholder.
services.source: UK police force published Grade 1/immediate response targets, order-of-magnitude cross-check
services.turnoutSource: UK police Grade 1/immediate-response dispatch-to-mobile activation norms, order-of-magnitude cross-check against multiple force performance reports -- this schema takes 2.0 min as a derived mid-range figure (patrol officers are typically already mobile, but call-handling/dispatch relay adds this leg).
services.turnoutConfidenceNote: Derived order-of-magnitude, not one measured national standard.

ambulance.source: derived approximation, cross-checked against NHS England ambulance incident volume statistics (~10,000-11,000 daily incidents per million population order-of-magnitude nationally)

fire.source: derived approximation, cross-checked against Home Office Fire & Rescue incident statistics

police.source: derived approximation, cross-checked against ONS/Home Office recorded-crime and incident-response order-of-magnitude

combinedTotalPer1000PerDay.note: Sum of the three services above; this is the figure scale_ladder.json's emergencyIncidentsPerDay is derived from.

speedDegradation.$comment: Emergency vehicles partially bypass congestion (priority signals, lane-splitting/hard-shoulder, oncoming-lane use) but are not immune, especially at high v/c and on narrow single-lane classes without an escape lane.

curve.note: matches the existing webconsole 0.75 saturation threshold (FEAT-2326609772/data.ts CONGESTION_CONSTANTS) as the point where emergency response first meaningfully degrades
gridlock; even priority bypass mostly fails

narrowClassPenalty.note: single-lane/narrow classes offer no bypass lane for priority vehicles to use, applied on top of the vOverC curve

speedDegradation.interpolationRule: Piecewise-linear interpolation between the listed vOverC anchor points; clamp to the curve's endpoints outside [0.0, 1.25].

provenance.source: NHS England ARP, UK Fire & Rescue Service IRMP first-attendance targets, UK police Grade 1 response targets, Home Office/ONS incident-rate statistics
provenance.note: Targets carry measured provenance (published national/force standards); incident rates and the speed-degradation curve are derived approximations pending Aaron's balance pass.
